Alert complexity and placement volatility, pooled or by fiscal year

Source: R/cxvol.R
cxvol.Rd

The analysis of Ruhela (2026) on any release of Ontario's restrictive confinement records: from the person-year table (otpyr()) it gives, for the years pooled or for each fiscal year, the share of person-years with complex alert profiles (cx = 1), mean placement volatility by group, the crude Poisson rate ratio (the ratio of the two means, infinite when every count without complex alerts is 0), the one-to-one nearest-neighbour propensity matching without replacement of each complex person-year to a control on age group, gender and fiscal year (cbatt(), in 'MatchIt”s default order), the count model on the matched frame with a random intercept per regional cluster (cntmix()), and the bounds on the average effect on the matched frame with no assumption and under monotone treatment response and selection (mtrbnd()).

Usage

cxvol(x, by = c("pool", "year"), yterm = TRUE, fam = c("nb", "poisson"), ...)

Arguments

x

A person-year table from otpyr(), or what otpyr() takes (a data frame of the release or a table key).

by

"pool" for the years together, "year" for each year.

yterm

TRUE to adjust for the fiscal year in the pooled propensity and count models.

fam

The family of cntmix().

...

Passed to otpyr() when x is not a person-year table.

Value

An object of class cxvol, a list: res, one row per sample (sample, n, n1, share, vm, vm1, vm0, crude, nm, vm1m, vm0m, irr, lo, hi, est, se, p, ncl, fam, mlo, mhi, bhi: the Manski bounds and the upper bound under both monotonicity assumptions, whose lower bound is 0; ymax, the largest count on the matched frame, the range used by the bounds; note, why the rate ratio has no estimate when it has none, such as a group whose counts on the matched frame are all 0, else ""); fits, the cntmix() fits; by; yterm.

Details

A single fiscal year cannot identify a year term: by = "pool" with one year and yterm = TRUE is refused; by = "year" drops the term in each year and says so. A sample with no complex person-year, or none without, is refused, naming it.

References

Ruhela, V. S. (2026). Alert complexity and placement volatility in Ontario restrictive confinement data. Major research paper, Centre for Criminology and Sociolegal Studies, University of Toronto.

Examples

set.seed(4)
n <- 600
p <- data.frame(year = sample(2025:2026, n, TRUE),
                gender = sample(c("Male", "Female"), n, TRUE, c(9, 1)),
                age = sample(c("18 to 24", "25 to 49", "50+"), n, TRUE),
                rc = sample(c("A", "B", "A + B", "C"), n, TRUE),
                cx = rbinom(n, 1, 0.2))
p$vm <- rpois(n, exp(-2 + 0.3 * p$cx + (p$rc == "A + B")))
cxvol(p, fam = "poisson")
#> cxvol: alert complexity (cx) and placement volatility (vm), years pooled
#>     sample   n     cx    vm1    vm0 crude matched    irr     lo    hi     p
#>  2025-2026 600 0.1917 0.2174 0.2062 1.054     230 0.8477 0.5012 1.434 0.538
#>     bound
#>  -0.06087
#> irr: rate ratio of the matched count model (poisson); bound: upper end of [0, bound] under monotone response and
#> selection (below 0, the data contradict the two assumptions)
